idempotency_key.description: Optional client-supplied key. A request repeated with the same key is never executed again: the service returns the original outcome. Reuse the key when retrying the same request.

args.title: checkout-api v2.3.1 failing health checks; rolled back to v2.3.0
args.summary: checkout-api v2.3.1 (latest deploy) was failing health checks in all production regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west) with an 18% error rate. Rolled back to v2.3.0, the most recent release that was healthy in production. The first rollback attempt halted after us-east because of an orchestrator error, which left the regions on mixed versions (us-east v2.3.0, us-west/eu-west v2.3.1). A retry finished the rollout. All three regions are now on v2.3.0 and healthy, with a 0.2% error rate. Follow-ups: find the root cause of the v2.3.1 failure (its v2.3.1-rc build was also unhealthy in staging) and look into the orchestrator error during rollout.

trace.final:
checkout-api is rolled back to v2.3.0 in all regions, it's healthy again, and SEV2 incident INC-0001 is open.

- **Rollback:** v2.3.0 is the most recent release that was healthy in production. v2.3.1, the latest deploy, was failing health checks with an 18% error rate.
  - The first rollback stopped partway because of an orchestrator error. Only us-east switched to v2.3.0, while us-west and eu-west stayed on v2.3.1.
  - Rolling back to a fixed version is safe to repeat, so I ran it again and it finished.
  - All three regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west) are now on v2.3.0, and the error rate is down to 0.2%.
- **Incident:** INC-0001 is open as SEV2 and the on-call engineer has been paged.
  - The first attempt to open it timed out. I retried with the same ID so it couldn't create a duplicate, and confirmed there's only one incident.
  - It describes the bad release, the rollback, and the failed first attempt. It also lists two follow-ups: find out why v2.3.1 failed (its test build v2.3.1-rc was also unhealthy in staging) and look into the orchestrator error.

No change-manager approval was needed, because v2.3.0 has been healthy in production before.

content.text: Only us-east got rolled back. Rolling back to a fixed version is safe to repeat, so I'll try once more to finish the remaining regions.
